raw.overview: All three advisors unanimously confirm that the sign-on bonus repayment clause in Clause 6b requires full 100% gross repayment of the $40,000 bonus if resignation occurs within 24 months, with no proration provision, directly violating the user's constraint that repayment obligations must expire by Month 12 (or be prorated monthly) to prevent an out-of-pocket clawback at Month 18.
raw.points_of_note: The advisors consistently cite the 24-month repayment window with 100% gross obligation as the core conflict with the Month 12 expiration requirement, noting that leaving at Month 18 would trigger full repayment without proration, creating an unavoidable out-of-pocket cash clawback; while Advisor 1 specifically questions whether Clause 6b contains any expiration date or pro-rata schedule, Advisors 2 and 3 explicitly confirm the unprorated 24-month term violates the user's constraint without offering alternative interpretations.
raw.suggested_next_step: Proceed to negotiate Clause 6b to amend the repayment period from 24 months to 12 months or introduce monthly proration of the net after-tax payout to satisfy the user's constraint and eliminate the Month 18 clawback risk.

consensus.text:
ASSESSMENT OVERVIEW: All three advisors unanimously confirm that the sign-on bonus repayment clause in Clause 6b requires full 100% gross repayment of the $40,000 bonus if resignation occurs within 24 months, with no proration provision, directly violating the user's constraint that repayment obligations must expire by Month 12 (or be prorated monthly) to prevent an out-of-pocket clawback at Month 18.
POINTS OF NOTE: The advisors consistently cite the 24-month repayment window with 100% gross obligation as the core conflict with the Month 12 expiration requirement, noting that leaving at Month 18 would trigger full repayment without proration, creating an unavoidable out-of-pocket cash clawback; while Advisor 1 specifically questions whether Clause 6b contains any expiration date or pro-rata schedule, Advisors 2 and 3 explicitly confirm the unprorated 24-month term violates the user's constraint without offering alternative interpretations.
SUGGESTED NEXT STEP: Proceed to negotiate Clause 6b to amend the repayment period from 24 months to 12 months or introduce monthly proration of the net after-tax payout to satisfy the user's constraint and eliminate the Month 18 clawback risk.
